description: A waveshaper that runs a signal through the first nine Chebyshev polynomials at once, each acting as a frequency multiplier on a sine input

params.text: Sets how much of that polynomial's output goes into the mixed output, from none to all of it
Chooses the range the input is read over: -5 / +5 for a signal centred on zero, or 0 / +10 for one that never goes below zero

outputs.text: The input through the first Chebyshev polynomial, which leaves a sine at its own frequency
The input through the second Chebyshev polynomial, which doubles the frequency of a sine
The input through the third Chebyshev polynomial, which trebles the frequency of a sine
The input through the fourth Chebyshev polynomial, which multiplies the frequency of a sine by four
The input through the fifth Chebyshev polynomial, which multiplies the frequency of a sine by five
The input through the sixth Chebyshev polynomial, which multiplies the frequency of a sine by six
The input through the seventh Chebyshev polynomial, which multiplies the frequency of a sine by seven
The input through the eighth Chebyshev polynomial, which multiplies the frequency of a sine by eight
The input through the ninth Chebyshev polynomial, which multiplies the frequency of a sine by nine
The weighted sum of the nine shaped signals, set by the SERIES MIXER knobs

notes: the frequency multiplying only holds for a sine input at full scale; a quieter or more complex input gives a different set of harmonics.
the nine mixer knobs are added up, and if they total more than 1 the mix is divided by that total, so turning knobs up past that point redistributes the mix rather than making it louder.
the module starts with the first knob at 0.2 and the rest at 0.1, which totals exactly 1 and leaves the mix unscaled.
the input is clamped to the chosen range before shaping, so a signal outside it is flattened rather than folded.
the even-numbered polynomials add a constant term, so their outputs carry a DC offset.

inputs.0:
continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
